3-125.pali_snippet: Tathā hi mahāanuḷatthero nāma sambahule bhikkhū piṇḍāya caritvā sukkhabhattameva labhitvā gaṅgātīre nisīditvā paribhuñjamāne disvā gaṅgāya udakaṃ sappimaṇḍanti adhiṭṭhahitvā sāmaṇerānaṃ saññaṃ adāsi.

9-1.english_snippet: 47. viii. The forest-dweller’s practice is undertaken with one of the following statements: “I refuse an abode in a village” or “I undertake the forest-dweller’s practice.”
9-1.pali_snippet: 31.Āraññikaṅgampi "gāmantasenāsanaṃ paṭikkhipāmi, āraññikaṅgaṃ samādiyāmī"ti imesaṃ aññataravacanena samādinnaṃ hoti.

9-10.pali_snippet: Araññaṃ pana vinayapariyāye tāva "ṭhapetvā gāmañca gāmūpacārañca sabbametaṃ arañña"nti (pārā. 92) vuttaṃ.

9-11.english_snippet: According to the Abhidhamma method it is described thus: “Having gone out beyond the boundary post, all that is forest” (Vibh 251; Paṭis I 176).

9-12.english_snippet: But according to the Suttanta method its characteristic is this: “A forest abode is five hundred bow-lengths distant” (Vin IV 183).
9-12.pali_snippet: Imasmiṃ pana suttantikapariyāye "āraññakaṃ nāma senāsanaṃ pañcadhanusatikaṃ pacchima"nti idaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ.

7-74.english_snippet: And one of greedy temperament spreads his bed unhurriedly, lies down slowly, composing his limbs, and he sleeps in a confident manner. When woken, instead of getting up quickly, he gives his answer slowly as though doubtful.
7-74.pali_snippet: Rāgacarito ca ataramāno samaṃ seyyaṃ paññapetvā saṇikaṃ nipajjitvā aṅgapaccaṅgāni samodhāya pāsādikena ākārena sayati, vuṭṭhāpiyamāno ca sīghaṃ avuṭṭhāya saṅkito viya saṇikaṃ paṭivacanaṃ deti.

7-75.english_snippet: One of hating temperament spreads his bed hastily anyhow; with his body flung down he sleeps with a scowl. When woken, he gets up quickly and answers as though annoyed.
7-75.pali_snippet: Dosacarito taramāno yathā vā tathā vā seyyaṃ paññapetvā pakkhittakāyo bhākuṭiṃ katvā sayati, vuṭṭhāpiyamāno ca sīghaṃ vuṭṭhāya kupito viya paṭivacanaṃ deti.

7-76.english_snippet: One of deluded temperament spreads his bed all awry and sleeps mostly face downwards with his body sprawling. When woken, he gets up slowly, saying, “Hum. ”
7-76.pali_snippet: Mohacarito dussaṇṭhānaṃ seyyaṃ paññapetvā vikkhittakāyo bahulaṃ adhomukho sayati, vuṭṭhāpiyamāno ca huṅkāraṃ karonto dandhaṃ vuṭṭhāti.

7-77.english_snippet: 90. Since those of faithful temperament, etc., are parallel to those of greedy temperament, etc., their postures are therefore like those described above.
7-77.pali_snippet: Saddhācaritādayo pana yasmā rāgacaritādīnaṃ sabhāgā, tasmā tesampi tādisova iriyāpatho hotīti.

7-78.english_snippet: This firstly is how the temperaments may be recognized by the posture.

7-79.english_snippet: 91.By the action: also in the acts of sweeping, etc., one of greedy temperament grasps the broom well, and he sweeps cleanly and evenly without hurrying or scattering the sand, as if he were strewing sinduvāra flowers.
7-79.pali_snippet: Kiccāti sammajjanādīsu ca kiccesu rāgacarito sādhukaṃ sammajjaniṃ gahetvā ataramāno vālikaṃ avippakiranto sinduvārakusumasantharamiva santharanto suddhaṃ samaṃ sammajjati.

7-8.english_snippet: Greed seeks out sense desires as object, while faith seeks out the special qualities of virtue and so on.
7-8.pali_snippet: Yathā rāgo vatthukāme pariyesati, evaṃ saddhā sīlādiguṇe.

7-80.english_snippet: One of hating temperament grasps the broom tightly, and he sweeps uncleanly and unevenly with a harsh noise, hurriedly throwing up the sand on each side.
7-80.pali_snippet: Dosacarito gāḷhaṃ sammajjaniṃ gahetvā taramānarūpo ubhato vālikaṃ ussārento kharena saddena asuddhaṃ visamaṃ sammajjati.

7-81.english_snippet: One of deluded temperament grasps the broom loosely, and he sweeps neither cleanly nor evenly, mixing the sand up and turning it over.
7-81.pali_snippet: Mohacarito sithilaṃ sammajjaniṃ gahetvā samparivattakaṃ āḷolayamāno asuddhaṃ visamaṃ sammajjati.

7-82.english_snippet: 92.As with sweeping, so too with any action such as washing and dyeing robes, and so on. One of greedy temperament acts skilfully, gently, evenly and carefully.

7-84.english_snippet: One of deluded temperament acts unskilfully as if muddled, unevenly and indecisively.

7-85.english_snippet: Also one of greedy temperament wears his robe neither too tightly nor too loosely, confidently and level all round.

7-87.english_snippet: One of deluded temperament wears it loosely and in a muddled way.

7-88.english_snippet: Those of faithful temperament, etc., should be understood in the same way as those just described, since they are parallel.

7-89.english_snippet: This is how the temperaments may be recognized by the actions.

7-90.english_snippet: 93.By eating: One of greedy temperament likes eating rich sweet food. When eating, he makes a round lump not too big and eats unhurriedly, savouring the various tastes. He enjoys getting something good.

7-91.english_snippet: One of hating temperament likes eating rough sour food. When eating he makes a lump that fills his mouth, and he eats hurriedly without savouring the taste. He is aggrieved when he gets something not good.
7-91.pali_snippet: Dosacarito lūkhaambilabhojanappiyo hoti, bhuñjamāno ca mukhapūrakaṃ ālopaṃ katvā arasapaṭisaṃvedī taramāno bhuñjati, kiñcideva ca asāduṃ labhitvā domanassaṃ āpajjati.

7-92.english_snippet: One of deluded temperament has no settled choice. When eating, he makes a small un-rounded lump, and as he eats he drops bits into his dish, smearing his face, with his mind astray, thinking of this and that.

7-93.english_snippet: Also those of faithful temperament, etc., should be understood in the same way as those just described since they are parallel.

7-94.english_snippet: This is how the temperament may be recognized by eating.

1-12.pali_snippet: Vemajjhe chinnassa chavasarīrassetamadhivacanaṃ.

1-15.english_snippet: This is a term for a corpse in that particular state.
1-15.pali_snippet: Tathārūpassa chavasarīrassetamadhivacanaṃ.

1-16.english_snippet: 6.The scattered: what is strewed about (vividhaṃ khittaṃ) is scattered (vikkhittaṃ). What is scattered is the same as “the scattered” (vikkhittaka).
1-16.pali_snippet: Vividhaṃ khittaṃ vikkhittaṃ, vikkhittameva vikkhittakaṃ.

1-17.english_snippet: Or alternatively, what is scattered (vikkhitta) is vile (kucchita) because of repulsiveness, thus it is “the scattered” (vikkhittaka).
1-17.pali_snippet: Paṭikkūlattā vā kucchitaṃ vikkhittanti vikkhittakaṃ.

1-18.english_snippet: This is a term for a corpse that is strewed here and there in this way: “Here a hand, there a foot, there the head” (cf. M I 58).
1-18.pali_snippet: Aññena hatthaṃ aññena pādaṃ aññena sīsanti evaṃ tato tato khittassa chavasarīrassetamadhivacanaṃ.

1-19.english_snippet: 7. The hacked and scattered: it is hacked, and it is scattered in the way just described, thus it is “hacked and scattered” (hata-vikkhittaka).

1-2.english_snippet: Or alternatively, what is bloated (uddhumāta) is vile (kucchita) because of repulsiveness, thus it is “the bloated” (uddhumātaka).

1-20.english_snippet: This is a term for a corpse scattered in the way just described after it has been hacked with a knife in a crow’s-foot pattern on every limb.
1-20.pali_snippet: Kākapadākārena aṅgapaccaṅgesu satthena hanitvā vuttanayena vikkhittassa chavasarīrassetamadhivacanaṃ.

1-21.english_snippet: 8. The bleeding: it sprinkles (kirati), scatters, blood (lohita), and it trickles here and there, thus it is “the bleeding” (lohitaka).

1-22.english_snippet: This is a term for a corpse smeared with trickling blood.

1-24.english_snippet: This is a term for a corpse full of maggots.

1-27.english_snippet: This is a term both for a single bone and for a framework of bones.

2-25.english_snippet: In the place where the bloated sign of foulness has been left he notes any stone or termite-mound or tree or bush or creeper there each with its particular sign and in relation to the object.
2-25.pali_snippet: Yasmiṃ padese uddhumātakaṃ asubhanimittaṃ nikkhittaṃ hoti, tasmiṃ padese pāsāṇaṃ vā vammikaṃ vā rukkhaṃ vā gacchaṃ vā lataṃ vā sanimittaṃ karoti, sārammaṇaṃ karoti.

2-26.english_snippet: When he has done this, he characterizes the bloated sign of foulness by the fact of its having attained that particular individual essence. (see §84) by its colour, by its mark, by its shape, by its direction, by its location, by its delimi
2-26.pali_snippet: Sanimittaṃ katvā sārammaṇaṃ katvā uddhumātakaṃ asubhanimittaṃ sabhāvabhāvato upalakkheti, vaṇṇatopi liṅgatopi saṇṭhānatopi disatopi okāsatopi paricchedatopi sandhito vivarato ninnato thalato samantato.

2-27.english_snippet: Then he sees that the sign is properly apprehended, that it is properly remembered, that it is properly defined (as before).
2-27.pali_snippet: So taṃ nimittaṃ suggahitaṃ karoti, sūpadhāritaṃ upadhāreti, suvavatthitaṃ vavatthapeti.

2-37.english_snippet: 22.“When he has established reverence for it by seeing its advantages and by perceiving it as a treasure and so come to love it, he anchors his mind upon that object: ‘Surely in this way I shall be liberated from ageing and death.’
2-37.pali_snippet: "So ānisaṃsadassāvī ratanasaññī hutvā cittīkāraṃ upaṭṭhapetvā sampiyāyamāno tasmiṃ ārammaṇe cittaṃ upanibandhati 'addhā imāya paṭipadāya jarāmaraṇamhā parimuccissāmī'ti.

2-38.english_snippet: Quite secluded from sense desires, secluded from unprofitable things he enters upon and dwells in the first jhāna … [seclusion].

2-48.english_snippet: So instead of approaching it upwind, he should go downwind.

2-49.english_snippet: If he cannot go by a downwind path—if there is a mountain or a ravine or a rock or a fence or a patch of thorns or water or a bog in the way—then he should go stopping his nose with the corner of his robe.

2-5.english_snippet: 14. Why not?

2-50.english_snippet: These are the duties in going.

2-51.english_snippet: 26.When he has gone there in this way, he should not at once look at the sign of foulness;
2-51.pali_snippet: 107.Evaṃ gatena pana na tāva asubhanimittaṃ oloketabbaṃ.

2-52.english_snippet: he should make sure of the direction.

2-53.english_snippet: For perhaps if he stands in a certain direction, the object does not appear clearly to him and his mind is not wieldy.

2-55.english_snippet: And he should avoid standing to leeward or to windward of it.

2-57.english_snippet: and if he stands to windward and non-human beings are dwelling there, they may get annoyed and do him a mischief.

2-58.english_snippet: So he should move round a little and not stand too much to windward.

2-84.pali_snippet: Saṇṭhānato uddhumātakassa saṇṭhānavaseneva idamassa sīsasaṇṭhānaṃ, idaṃ gīvāsaṇṭhānaṃ, idaṃ hatthasaṇṭhānaṃ, idaṃ udarasaṇṭhānaṃ, idaṃ nābhisaṇṭhānaṃ, idaṃ kaṭisaṇṭhānaṃ, idaṃ ūrusaṇṭhānaṃ, idaṃ jaṅghāsaṇṭhānaṃ, idaṃ pādasaṇṭhānanti vavatth
